items.title: Scott Robinson interviewed by Monk Rowe,Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997
items.q: And so Randy Sandke does a lot of Bix’s music and Trumbauer and all of that, and he knows I play the C melody too, so I get to sort of be the Trumbauer-Rollini amalgam in those concerts.

ctx.x: Wow. And you’ve been using that on some of the classic jazz, as we see in that recent Jazz Times picture, which is really nice, which we’ll probably insert in this video. Tell me about that particular concert and what is the function of the bass saxophone in that classic jazz?

Well that’s where the instrument has seen its primary use. Of course Adrian Rollini is the acknowledged master of the bass saxophone. He played in the ‘20s on all those great records with Bix Beiderbecke and so that represents sort of the standard by which that type of use of the instrument is measured. And so Randy Sandke does a lot of Bix’s music and Trumbauer and all of that, and he knows I play the C melody too, so I get to sort of be the Trumbauer-Rollini amalgam in those concerts. And it’s a lot of fun. But…
No kidding. Can you see bringing one of those to these kind of festivals some day?
